EvidenceSchema.description:
Wire tag of the knowledge documents. Wave K1 writes `evidence.v2`; `evidence.v1` (C0) documents
are still read. An addition of v2 (a field, a relation, a concept node, a new document type) is
refused under the v1 tag, so a v1 reader never receives a document it would misread.

oneOf.description: C0. Still read; new documents are written as v2.
Every keyframe of the recording (the whole file was read).

Keyframes found by byte-range probes a few seconds of presentation time apart; enough for
keyframe-aligned segments and I-frame scrubbing, not a list of every keyframe.

KeyframeEntry.description: One keyframe of an MPEG-TS recording.

length.description:
Bytes from `offset` to the next video PES start: the keyframe's access unit plus the
packets of other streams interleaved with it (whole packets). The I-frame byte range.

offset.description: Byte offset of the TS packet that starts the keyframe's PES.

pts_s.description: Presentation time in seconds (90 kHz PTS, 33-bit wraps unwrapped by the indexer).

Origin.description:
Who produced a payload. `synthetic_fixture` marks hand-made contract examples; such payloads (and
anything computed from them) can never be presented as NASA results or qualify a model.
Produced-by-the-system payloads are `system` even when their *data* is synthetic (that is
`EvidenceClass::Synthetic` / `TrainedOn::Synthetic`).

VideoCodec.description: Video codec of an indexed MPEG-TS recording.

description:
Keyframe index of one `.ts` source version (R11), the input of M12's byte-range HLS
playlists. Written by `ignis sources media keyframes`, read by `/api/v1/sources/{id}/â€¦m3u8`.

bytes_read.description: Bytes the indexer read to build this index (byte ranges, not the whole file).

end_pts_s.description: Presentation time where the last frame ends (last PTS + one frame duration).

init_bytes.description:
Length of the leading packets up to and including the first PMT (whole packets): the
playlists' initialization section (`EXT-X-MAP`).

size_bytes.description: Size of the indexed object; a source of another size makes the index stale.
